{{Short description|American fluid mechanist}}
'''Sivaramakrishnan Balachandar''' is a [[professor]] at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]. Sivaramakrishnan  is an American physicist, a Distinguished Professor and William F. Powers Professor at University of Florida.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mae.ufl.edu/people/profiles/bala-balachandar/|title = S. "Bala" Balachandar » People – Department of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fora.aa.ufl.edu/provost/IndependentFora/Distinguished-Professors|title = Provost Independent Fora - Distinguished Professors/Curators}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=n1qenYwAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra|title = S. Balachandar}}</ref><ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211208/msUKv1NhjbA Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20210118163940/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msUKv1NhjbA Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite AV media| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msUKv1NhjbA| title = Bala Balachandar's Comedy Minute | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Balachandar has contributed to the understanding of [[thermal convection]] in the Earth's [[Mantle (geology)|mantle]], the structure of bluff body wakes and their effect on the dynamics of small particles, the dynamics of [[vortex|vortices]] in wall turbulence, and the theory of [[two-phase flow]], including the equilibrium [[Euler]] formulation for dispersion force.

He was made a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> after being nominated by their Division of [[Fluid Dynamics]] in 2006.,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2006&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2006|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> and he received the Francois Naftali Frenkiel Award from the American Physical Society Division of Fluid Dynamics in 1996<ref>Official biography at University of Florida Center for Compressible Multiphase Turbulence [https://www.eng.ufl.edu/ccmt/people/faculty/]</ref>   He is also a fellow  of the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]].

==Publications==
His most cited articles <ref name=GS>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=n1qenYwAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra] Google Scholar Author page, Accessed 13 January 2012  2021</ref> are:
*Jigen Zhou, Ronald J Adrian, S Balachandar, TM Kendall. Mechanisms for generating coherent packets of hairpin vortices in channel flow    (1999) ''[[Journal of Fluid Mechanics]]'' 387:353-396 (cited 1902 times)
* S Balachandar, JK Eaton. Turbulent dispersed multiphase flow (2010) ''[[Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics]]'' 42, 111–133. (cited 1200 times)
*P. Chakraborty, S Balachandar, RJ Adrian, On the relationships between local vortex identification schemes (2005) ''Journal of fluid mechanics'' 535: 189	(838	citations) 
*H Aref, S Balachandar  Chaotic advection in a Stokes flow  (1986)  ''[[Physics of Fluids]]'' 29 (11), 3515-3521	(344 citations)
*J.  Robichaux, S Balachandar, SP Vanka. Three-dimensional Floquet instability of the wake of square cylinder. (1999) ''Physics of Fluids'' 11 (3), 560-578	(331	citations)
* R Mittal, S Balachandar  Effect of three‐dimensionality on the lift and drag of nominally two‐dimensional cylinders ''Physics of Fluids'' 7 (8), 1841-18 (295 citations)
